Based on my search, here is a comprehensive overview of the bones of the head (skull):

## Overview

The human skull consists of **22 bones** (or 29 if including the inner ear bones and hyoid bone). These bones are primarily connected by immovable fibrous joints called **sutures**. The skull is divided into two main parts: the **cranium (neurocranium)** that encloses and protects the brain, and the **facial skeleton (viscerocranium)** that forms the face.

---

## Cranium (Neurocranium) — 8 Bones

The cranium forms the protective housing for the brain and consists of:

| Bone | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Frontal bone** (1) | Forms the forehead and superior portion of the eye sockets; contains frontal sinuses |
| **Parietal bones** (2) | Form the sides and roof of the cranial vault; meet at the sagittal suture |
| **Occipital bone** (1) | Forms the back and base of the skull; contains the **foramen magnum** where the spinal cord passes through |
| **Temporal bones** (2) | Form the sides and base of the cranium; house structures of the middle and inner ear; features include the mastoid process and styloid process |
| **Sphenoid bone** (1) | Butterfly-shaped bone at the base of the skull; contains the sella turcica (houses pituitary gland); articulates with almost every other cranial bone |
| **Ethmoid bone** (1) | Located between the orbits; forms part of the nasal cavity; contains the cribriform plate for olfactory nerves |

The cranium can be further subdivided into:
- **Calvaria (skullcap)** — the roof, formed by frontal, parietal, and occipital bones
- **Cranial base** — the floor, comprising parts of frontal, ethmoid, sphenoid, occipital, parietal, and temporal bones

---

## Facial Skeleton (Viscerocranium) — 14 Bones

| Bone | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Mandible** (1) | The lower jaw; largest and strongest facial bone; only movable bone of the skull |
| **Maxillae** (2) | Upper jaw bones; form most of the hard palate and part of the orbit; contain maxillary sinuses |
| **Zygomatic bones** (2) | Cheekbones; form part of the lateral walls of the orbits |
| **Nasal bones** (2) | Form the bridge of the nose |
| **Lacrimal bones** (2) | Small bones in the medial walls of the orbits; house the lacrimal sac |
| **Palatine bones** (2) | Form the posterior part of the hard palate and part of the nasal cavity |
| **Inferior nasal conchae** (2) | Curved bones projecting into the nasal cavity; aid in airflow regulation |
| **Vomer** (1) | Forms the inferior portion of the nasal septum |

---

## Major Cranial Sutures

- **Coronal suture** — between frontal and parietal bones
- **Sagittal suture** — between the two parietal bones
- **Lambdoid suture** — between parietal and occipital bones
- **Squamous suture** — between parietal and temporal bones

---

## Associated Bones (Not Part of Skull Proper)

- **Hyoid bone** — located in the neck; provides attachment for tongue and larynx muscles
- **Auditory ossicles** (malleus, incus, stapes) — tiny bones in the middle ear for sound transmission

---

## Key Functions

1. **Protection** — shields the brain, eyes, and other sensory organs
2. **Support** — provides structural framework for facial features
3. **Passageways** — numerous foramina allow nerves and blood vessels to pass through

Sources:
1. https://www.kenhub.com/en/library/anatomy/the-skull
2. https://www.osmosis.org/learn/Bones_of_the_cranium
3. https://teachmeanatomy.info/head/osteology/skull/
4. https://www.numberanalytics.com/blog/skull-bones-anatomy-histology-explored
5. https://www.acibademhealthpoint.com/the-back-of-head-bones-understanding-cranial-anatomy/
6. https://anatomynote.com/the-human-skull-an-anatomical-masterpiece/
7. https://anatomy.co.uk/skull
